title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: pricing and rounding of the final demurrage line
content:
## Scope

Under the AHL Demurrage and Detention Free Time category, this rule sets how the billed demurrage days of a per-container record are priced and brought together into the amount of its final demurrage line.

## Rule

1. Each demurrage day is billed at the demurrage rate of its slab and of the container's rate class for the product on the record.
2. Where a dangerous-goods uplift applies, it raises each day rate before the days are added.
3. The day rates so obtained are added up, and only the sum is rounded to the cent.

## The amount in words

Take the slab 1 days multiplied by the slab 1 demurrage rate, and likewise the slab 2, slab 3 and slab 4 days each multiplied by their own rate; total them; where an uplift applies, increase that total by the uplift percentage of itself (which is the same as raising every day rate by that percentage); and round that figure to the cent once, at the end.

## Worked example (hypothetical day rate of USD 33.33 and an illustrative uplift of 35 percent)

Three demurrage days in the same slab on a dangerous-goods booking: each uplifted day rate is USD 44.9955, and the three together come to USD 134.9865, rounded once to USD 134.99.

| Reading | Line amount |
|---|---|
| Correct: add the uplifted day rates, round the sum once | USD 134.99 |
| Wrong: round each day to USD 45.00 before adding | USD 135.00 |
